descripcion: At B1 you speculate with may, might and probably to talk about what might happen. The full speculation chain used at C1 comes later — a simple, graded prediction naming how sure you are is enough here.

ejemplos.texto: It might rain later, so take a jacket.
This will probably take a while.
It's definitely going to be busy tomorrow.

notas: Might and may express a real but uncertain possibility.
Probably usually goes between the subject and the verb: it will probably rain.
Definitely is used for a very confident prediction.

contraste.es: Quizás and probablemente correspond to maybe and probably, and the Spanish future to will, so graded certainty transfers well.
contraste.de: Vielleicht and wahrscheinlich correspond to maybe and probably, and wird to will. Careful: ich will means I want, not I will.
contraste.it: Forse and probabilmente correspond to maybe and probably, and the Italian future to will, so graded certainty transfers well.
contraste.fr: Peut-être and probablement correspond to maybe and probably, and the French future to will, so graded certainty transfers well.
contraste.pt: Talvez takes the subjunctive (talvez chova), which can lead to maybe it rains instead of maybe it'll rain. Provavelmente corresponds to probably.

errores: Using will for everything, without varying the certainty.
Using definitely for something that's actually uncertain.
autochequeo: Have I used more than one certainty word, not just will?
Is probably in the right position?
Does the certainty level match how sure I really am?
Does the phrase sound polite and natural?
Does the phrase sound polite and natural?
promptCorreccion: Focus only on the words used to express certainty in a prediction. Check the position of probably and whether the level of certainty is accurate. Do not rewrite the text.

es: *A lo mejor* rendered as *At the best* instead of *Maybe* or *Perhaps*.
de: *Es kann sein, dass er kommt* rendered as *It can be that he comes* instead of *He might come*.
it: *Può darsi che venga* rendered as *It can be that he comes* instead of *He might come*.
fr: *Il se peut qu'il vienne* rendered as *It can be that he comes* instead of *He might come*.
pt: *Se calhar* rendered as *If it happens* instead of *Maybe* or *Perhaps*.
